intervention: Keep identical predictive files, instrument states, old acquisition plan and textual lessons; remove only the newly consolidated program and its manifest entry.
learning: Retrospective consolidation of a selected successful development experience. The LLM writes the procedure from paid actions and outcomes; no terminal results enter its context.
transfer: Freeze once before four independent prospective transfers. The LLM chooses whether to use or adapt a method. No transfer feedback enters another task.
terminal_order: Generate terminal labels only after all four transfer agents stop learning.
cost_scope: Record prior supplied learning, consolidation and transfer separately; include the same common learning cost once in each condition's complete sequence.
limitations: One learned procedure and one paired new apparatus. The removed method may be reconstructed from the shared textual lesson; this tests additional executable-method availability.
